links.outcome: Readability (FKGL) of LLM pediatric asthma outputs versus recommended patient reading level
links.effect: Mean FKGL across models was 13.2–14.9, far exceeding recommended reading level for patient materials; DeepSeek least readable, ChatGPT-4o most comprehensible (FRE diff 12.41, p=.005).
links.quote: Critically, the mean readability level of all outputs (FKGL: 13.2–14.9) far exceeded the recommended reading accessibility level for patient materials.

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of LLM outputs for patients
links.effect: All four LLMs failed to meet health-literacy standards; ChatGPT-4o was relatively more comprehensible; DeepSeek significantly worse than all other models (all p<.05).
links.quote: ChatGPT‑4o shows relative advantages in comprehensibility, yet none meet recommended health-literacy standards.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the clinical accuracy and readability of four commercial LLMs on pediatric asthma questions, evaluating off-the-shelf models without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
